name: com.autoview/mcp
title: Autoview
description: Place and inspect orders on your own exchange accounts from an MCP-connected agent.

tools.name: setup
tools.description: Read this FIRST. Returns your account overview: token scopes (live/exchange), which exchanges your token can call at all (callable), which of those allow a real live order right now vs. force a dry-run for lack of an active subscription (live_allowed/dry_run_forced, with upgrade_url when forced), per-exchange facts (id, whether it is free, whether it is a paper/no-real-money venue, whether the `link` tool accepts it (linkable), the parameters its integration lists as unsupported (unsupported_parameters), its setup_url and its required credential labels (credentials)), and your hooks with their linked exchanges. If no hook is linked to any exchange yet, recommended_first_exchange points at a free paper venue to start with. failing_hooks flags any hook whose last several alerts all failed with the SAME error (a stuck webhook loop). Requires your Autoview account token.

token.description: your Autoview account token — an av_mcp_ personal access token, generate one at /account/tokens/ on the Autoview site. Omit this if your MCP client already sends it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header (Claude Code, Cursor, and most non-browser clients do this automatically once configured).

tools.name: connect
tools.description: Connect any exchange configured on Autoview (see catalog) to your account: creates a webhook and links it to your already-saved credentials for that exchange, the same steps 2-4 the website's setup wizard runs. Safe to call more than once -- if a webhook is already linked, it reports connected:true and creates nothing new. If you have no credentials saved for this exchange yet, returns connect_url instead: open it in a browser to add them, then call connect again with the same exchange (for a paper/testnet exchange you can instead call link with its keys; real-money keys are browser-only). Connecting a real-money (non-paper) exchange requires a live-scoped token; any token can connect a paper/testnet exchange. Requires your Autoview account token.

token.description: your Autoview account token — an av_mcp_ personal access token, generate one at /account/tokens/ on the Autoview site. Omit this if your MCP client already sends it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header (Claude Code, Cursor, and most non-browser clients do this automatically once configured).

hook_id.description: link this specific existing hook instead of letting connect pick or create one (see the `hooks` tool for your hook ids). Must have no other exchange linked -- an order fires on every exchange a hook links, so connect refuses to add a second one; omit hook_id to get a dedicated hook

tools.name: link
tools.description: Save a PAPER/TESTNET exchange's API keys to your account and link them to a webhook, in one step -- for an agent that has a practice account's keys and no browser. Only ALPACAPAPER, BINANCEDELIVERYTESTNET, BINANCEFUTURESTESTNET, BINANCETEST, BITGETDEMO, BITGETMIXDEMO, BITMEXTESTNET, BYBITCOPYTESTNET, BYBITSPOTTESTNET, BYBITTESTNET, CAPITALDEMO, CRYPTODEMO, DERIBITTESTNET, GATEFUTURESTESTNET, GEMINISANDBOX, HYPERLIQUIDTESTNET, OANDAPRACTICE, OKXDEMO, OKXEEADEMO, OKXUSDEMO, TRADOVATESIM are accepted (they never move real money); real-money exchanges are refused whatever your token's scope, and their keys must be added on autoview.com in a browser (see connect). The credentials object uses named keys (public, private, passphrase, email, vault, id, cid, sec); which of them an exchange takes, and what each is called on that exchange, is in catalog({ exchange }): its credentials schema lists the exact keys (titles are the exchange's own labels) and which are required. The keys are encrypted and stored exactly as the website's setup form stores them, and are never echoed back. hook_id, if given, must be one of your own hooks with no exchange linked yet (an order fires on every exchange a hook links); omit it to use an empty hook of yours or get a new one. Then call entry with the returned hook_id (dry-run by default) to check the keys work. Requires your Autoview account token; any token can link a paper exchange.

token.description: your Autoview account token — an av_mcp_ personal access token, generate one at /account/tokens/ on the Autoview site. Omit this if your MCP client already sends it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header (Claude Code, Cursor, and most non-browser clients do this automatically once configured).

exchange.description: the paper/testnet exchange these keys belong to

public.description: ALPACAPAPER: API Key ID; BINANCEDELIVERYTESTNET: API Key; BINANCEFUTURESTESTNET: API Key; BINANCETEST: API Key; BITGETDEMO: Access API Key; BITGETMIXDEMO: Access API Key; BITMEXTESTNET: ID; BYBITCOPYTESTNET: API Key; BYBITSPOTTESTNET: API Key; BYBITTESTNET: API Key; CAPITALDEMO: API Key; CRYPTODEMO: API Key; DERIBITTESTNET: Access Key; GATEFUTURESTESTNET: API Key; GEMINISANDBOX: API Key; HYPERLIQUIDTESTNET: Public Address (optional); OKXDEMO: API Key; OKXEEADEMO: API Key; OKXUSDEMO: API Key; TRADOVATESIM: Username

private.description: ALPACAPAPER: Secret Key; BINANCEDELIVERYTESTNET: Secret; BINANCEFUTURESTESTNET: Secret; BINANCETEST: Secret; BITGETDEMO: Secret Key; BITGETMIXDEMO: Secret Key; BITMEXTESTNET: Secret; BYBITCOPYTESTNET: Private Key; BYBITSPOTTESTNET: Private Key; BYBITTESTNET: Private Key; CAPITALDEMO: Custom Password; CRYPTODEMO: Secret Key; DERIBITTESTNET: Access Secret; GATEFUTURESTESTNET: API Secret; GEMINISANDBOX: API Secret; HYPERLIQUIDTESTNET: Secret Key; OANDAPRACTICE: Access Token; OKXDEMO: Secret Key; OKXEEADEMO: Secret Key; OKXUSDEMO: Secret Key; TRADOVATESIM: Password

passphrase.description: BITGETDEMO: Passphrase; BITGETMIXDEMO: Passphrase; OKXDEMO: Passphrase; OKXEEADEMO: Passphrase; OKXUSDEMO: Passphrase

credentials.description: the practice account's keys, one string per field: fill only the fields the chosen exchange takes. The credentials object uses named keys (public, private, passphrase, email, vault, id, cid, sec); which of them an exchange takes, and what each is called on that exchange, is in catalog({ exchange }): its credentials schema lists the exact keys (titles are the exchange's own labels) and which are required.

hook_id.description: link this specific hook of yours (it must have no exchange linked yet); omit to use an empty hook or create a new one

tools.name: revoke_token
tools.description: Revoke the token this call is made with, so it stops working at once: every later call with it is refused. It only ever revokes the calling token (there is no target to pass), never another token of the account. Already revoked or expired counts as done (ok, already_revoked:true), not as an error. Needs the token's "Allow revoke and unlink" permission, which is off until your user ticks it at /account/tokens/. Requires your Autoview account token.

token.description: your Autoview account token — an av_mcp_ personal access token, generate one at /account/tokens/ on the Autoview site. Omit this if your MCP client already sends it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header (Claude Code, Cursor, and most non-browser clients do this automatically once configured).

tools.name: unlink
tools.description: Remove one of your hooks, the same as deleting it by hand on autoview.com: its exchange links, then the hook itself (alerts sent to its URL stop placing orders), then any saved exchange API keys no other hook still uses (real-money keys included; keys another hook links are kept). The token must be scoped for every exchange the hook links, and a hook linking a real-money exchange needs a live-scoped token, the same as connect. One transaction, all or nothing. A hook that is already gone, or is not on your account, is reported as ok with already_gone:true and nothing is deleted. Needs the token's "Allow revoke and unlink" permission, which is off until your user ticks it at /account/tokens/. Requires your Autoview account token.

token.description: your Autoview account token — an av_mcp_ personal access token, generate one at /account/tokens/ on the Autoview site. Omit this if your MCP client already sends it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header (Claude Code, Cursor, and most non-browser clients do this automatically once configured).

hook_id.description: the hook to remove: one of your hooks (see the `hooks` tool)

tools.name: catalog
tools.description: List every exchange configured on Autoview, filterable by paper (testnet/practice/sim, no real money), free (no Autoview subscription required), and name. Every listed exchange works with entry, command, alert and connect once its credentials are linked to one of your hooks (the exchange itself validates the order); linkable ones also take paper keys via link -- see connect_url to add credentials for one. Pass exchange (any spelling of its id, e.g. "OANDAPRACTICE") to get that one exchange in detail instead of the list: credentials is a JSON Schema whose property keys are exactly the keys link takes (titles are the exchange's own labels, required lists the ones it needs), plus linkable and unsupported_parameters (command parameters the exchange rejects, e.g. sl/tp; an attached bracket using one is refused up front). The list reply also carries language: the card for the one-line Autoview trade language that command({ line }) accepts. Requires your Autoview account token.

token.description: your Autoview account token — an av_mcp_ personal access token, generate one at /account/tokens/ on the Autoview site. Omit this if your MCP client already sends it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header (Claude Code, Cursor, and most non-browser clients do this automatically once configured).

paper.description: filter to (true) or exclude (false) paper/testnet/sim exchanges; omit for both

free.description: filter to (true) or exclude (false) exchanges that need no Autoview subscription; omit for both

name.description: case-insensitive substring match against the exchange's display name or id, e.g. "binance"

exchange.description: one exchange id (any spelling, e.g. "OANDAPRACTICE" or "oanda-practice") to get its credential schema and facts instead of the list; paper/free/name are ignored when this is set

tools.name: events
tools.description: Read what your orders did. Pass trace (the id entry or command's caller received) to read one order's events; omit trace to list your account's recent events instead, newest first, optionally narrowed by hook_id and/or canonical_id — this is the only way to see an order any webhook sender (TradingView, a script, another platform) fired directly, since it never went through entry and has no trace. Requires your Autoview account token. Poll this a moment after an order if the events are not there yet — the exchange reports back out-of-band.

token.description: your Autoview account token — an av_mcp_ personal access token, generate one at /account/tokens/ on the Autoview site. Omit this if your MCP client already sends it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header (Claude Code, Cursor, and most non-browser clients do this automatically once configured).

trace.description: the trace id returned by the entry tool for the order you want to inspect; omit to list your account's recent events instead

hook_id.description: when trace is omitted, narrow the account-wide listing to events reported for this hook

canonical_id.description: when trace is omitted, narrow the account-wide listing to events reported for one webhook delivery (the canonical id a webhook call produces)

tools.name: hooks
tools.description: List your Autoview webhook URLs: the address any webhook sender POSTs an alert to (a script or cron job, n8n, Zapier, your own server, or a TradingView alert's webhook field). The body is the command text from `command`, sent as plain text, a JSON string, or JSON {"alert": "..."} (form posts are refused). Each hook already knows which exchange(s) it is linked to; there is nothing further to configure on the Autoview side. Pair with the `command` tool (or use `alert` to build both at once). Requires your Autoview account token. The returned URL is itself a bearer secret for unattended trading — treat it like a password; rotate a hook's key from /account/hooks/ on the Autoview site if it leaks. Only a live-enabled token gets a URL with its key: a dry-run-only token gets each URL without it (keyed:true still says the hook needs one, key_note says why), and an exchange-scoped token lists only the hooks whose every linked exchange is in its scope (out_of_scope_hooks counts the rest).

token.description: your Autoview account token — an av_mcp_ personal access token, generate one at /account/tokens/ on the Autoview site. Omit this if your MCP client already sends it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header (Claude Code, Cursor, and most non-browser clients do this automatically once configured).

tools.name: command
tools.description: Build an Autoview alert command string from structured order fields (symbol, side, quantity, type, price, trigger), or from ONE line of the Autoview trade language (line, e.g. "buy(BTCUSD, 0.2, -0.5%)"; grammar in catalog's language card), without placing an order. A line reply also carries echo, one plain sentence stating the resolved order: confirm the sentence, not the string: the output is the alert body any webhook sender POSTs to a hook URL (for TradingView, the value create_alert's `message` field carries). Also builds cancel/close/flat management commands via `action` (see entry's description). Dry-run by default: a bare call returns a preview command (appends d=1); set live:true to build a command that trades for real once the alert fires. Pass the alert field instead to check and return raw webhook command text with any key a webhook accepts. Prefer the `alert` tool if you also need the destination webhook, expiration, and resolution in one call. Requires your Autoview account token; live:true requires a live-scoped token. exchange is optional: pass any exchange id configured on Autoview (see the `catalog` tool; a bracket is refused if that exchange lists sl/tp as unsupported); omit exchange entirely to build a generic command routed by whichever exchange(s) the destination hook is linked to.

token.description: your Autoview account token — an av_mcp_ personal access token, generate one at /account/tokens/ on the Autoview site. Omit this if your MCP client already sends it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header (Claude Code, Cursor, and most non-browser clients do this automatically once configured).

exchange.description: optional — any exchange id known to Autoview (see `catalog`); a bracket is refused if that exchange lists its params as unsupported; omit entirely to skip that check

line.description: one line of the Autoview trade language instead of the structured fields below, e.g. buy(BTCUSD, 0.2), buy(BTCUSD, 0.2, -0.5%), sell(BTCUSD, 0.2, stop(78000)), close(BTCUSD), link(buy(BTCUSD, 0.2, market), takeProfit(+500), stopLoss(-300)), link(buy(BTCUSD, 0.2, market), takeProfit(+5%), stopLoss(-3%)). Slots are symbol, size, price; a signed price is an offset from the ticker, an unsigned one is absolute; no type word = limit at the ticker; no key=value. Full card: catalog's language field. Do not combine with symbol/side/quantity/type/price/trigger/brackets.

alert.description: the raw command text a webhook body carries, e.g. s=BTCUSD b=buy q=0.01 fp=60000 ef=any tif=gtc; any key a webhook accepts works here, it is checked by the engine's parser and returned as-is (with d=1 leading each line unless live is true). Do not combine with line or the structured order fields.

symbol.description: the instrument symbol, e.g. EUR_USD, XBTUSD, BTC_USD, or the exchange-native symbol a TradingView EXCHANGE:TICKER maps to. Required unless line or alert is set

action.description: manage EXISTING orders/positions on symbol instead of placing a new one: cancel = cancel open orders, close = close open positions, flat = cancel every order AND close every position (Tradovate only). When set, side (if given) is an optional buy/sell filter (not applicable to flat), and quantity/type/price/trigger/brackets/unit are ignored.

side.description: order direction; required unless action is set, where it is an optional buy/sell filter for cancel/close (omit for flat)

quantity.description: order size: a positive number (contracts/units), or a percent-of-balance string like "50%" (1-100%). Required unless action is set.

type.description: order type; defaults to limit at the ticker (t=limit with no price, same as a plain alert). An attached bracket needs type market explicitly.

price.description: absolute limit price; required for an explicit limit, post_only, ioc, fok, and stop_limit (omit type and price for a limit at the ticker)

trigger.description: absolute trigger (stop) price; required for stop and stop_limit

priceRef.description: reference price for percent sizing and brackets

sizeAgainstEquity.description: for a percent quantity, size against equity instead of available balance (y=equity)

unit.description: "currency" treats quantity as a CURRENCY amount to convert to units at the resolved price (u=currency) — e.g. quantity:10 with unit:"currency" on BTC/USD buys $10 of BTC instead of 10 BTC. Only meaningful with a fixed (non-percent) quantity.

stopLoss.description: attached bracket stop-loss distance from the fill: points (10) or a percent string such as 3%; a sign, if given, must point the right way); pairs with takeProfit or a trail leg

takeProfit.description: attached bracket take-profit distance from the fill: points (20) or a percent string such as 5%; pairs with stopLoss or a trail leg

trailStop.description: auto-trail stop distance in points; requires trailActivate

trailActivate.description: points of profit before the trail starts; required whenever trailStop is set

trailFrequency.description: how often the trailing stop re-checks price; defaults to 1 if omitted

live.description: false (default) = build a dry-run preview command (appends d=1); true = build a command that places a real order when the alert fires

tools.name: explain_command
tools.description: Explain an existing Autoview command / alert message in plain English: what the engine will actually do with it on the named exchange (side, size, order type, price, brackets, account, dry run), plus caveats where that exchange quietly downgrades or ignores a key, or where the engine refuses the line. For example, Alpaca, Binance, Binance Delivery, ByBit Copy, Capital.com, Charles Schwab, OANDA and Tradovate have no post-only order, so the engine refuses t=post there and sends nothing, because the order would go out as a plain limit order that can fill at once; send t=limit for a plain limit. Accepts the classic key=value form (several lines, | or & legs included) or a one-line v3 call like buy(BTCUSD, 0.1, -1%). Returns { explanation: string, lines: [{ line, text, caveats: [{ text }], venue }] } or { error }. Read-only: it parses text only, never reads an account, a key, or sends anything. Describes, never recommends. No token, no account: works for a guest. To see a simulated fill beside the explanation, use sandbox_run.

token.description: not needed: explain_command reads no account data and ignores any token sent

command.description: the alert message / command string to explain, e.g. e=kraken s=BTCUSD b=buy q=0.1 p=-1% t=post

exchange.description: exchange id (any spelling) to explain against when a line carries no e=

tools.name: sandbox_run
tools.description:
Run one alert through Autoview's Alert Sandbox and see exactly what Autoview would do with it: the parsed orders and a simulated fill for each. No token, no account, no exchange key: simulation only, no real order is placed.

Send the order one of two ways: command (alert text: the classic key=value form "e=kraken s=BTCUSD b=buy q=0.01" or a v3 line "buy(BTCUSD, 0.01)"), or order (structured: { "exchange": "oanda", "symbol": "EURUSD", "side": "buy", "qty": 1000 }). Not both. A limit order is { ..., "type": "limit", "limit_price": 50000 }. order takes only exchange, symbol, side, qty, type and limit_price: order.price is refused (order_bad_field), because the top-level price is a different thing, the market price you read, not a limit. To close, send command with c=position (for example "e=kraken s=XBTUSD c=position") and the same sandbox_id: it closes that sandbox_id's paper position on the symbol at market, a long by a sell at the bid and a short by a buy at the ask.

Prices. Each fill is priced in this order and labelled with where the price came from (fill.origin): own_key (the user's own connected account; not available yet, coming), venue_ticker (the venue's free public ticker, e.g. Kraken, Coinbase, OKX, Bybit for crypto), caller (a price you pass in price), alert_fp (fp= in the alert, e.g. TradingView {{close}}). If Autoview has no price for the market (stocks, most forex, futures), read the price from your own user's data source and pass it as price (plus price_source and price_time); the fill is then labelled caller-supplied, never presented as Autoview's quote.

Returns { sandbox: true, real_order_placed: false, notice, sandbox_id, webhook_url, compiled?, orders: [{ exchange, side, symbol, qty, type, order_price?, fill }], explanation?, next }.

Fill shapes. A priced fill is { status: "filled", price, price_label, price_source, origin, origin_note, priced_at, price_age_ms, side_of_book?, limit?, price_warning?, caller_price_source?, caller_price_time? }. price_label is Autoview's short label for where the fill price came from, for example "Kraken XBTUSD best ask" (a venue fill at the ask) or "caller-supplied" (your price). price_source is the same label under its older name, kept for existing readers. The source and time you sent with a caller price are echoed in caller_price_source and caller_price_time. A market order, or a limit the book has reached (a buy limit at or above the ask, a sell limit at or below the bid; with a caller price, at or better than it), fills at the ask, bid or your price, never at the limit. price_warning is set when the price was more than 15 minutes old at receipt (for example "The caller price is 5h 2m old"): the fill still used it, so read a fresh price if you want a current fill. A limit the price has not reached is { status: "not_filled", price: null, reference_price, limit, price_label, side_of_book?, origin, origin_note, note, fix }: nothing filled and the sandbox never fills it later; do not pass price again, read fix. An unpriced fill is { status: "no_price", price: null, note, website_note?, price_error? }: price_error is { code, market, message, fix: [steps] }; follow the fix steps and call again. A c=position close with no open position on that symbol for this sandbox_id is { status: "nothing_to_close", price: null, note }: nothing was filled and there is nothing to fix.

price_error codes (in fill.price_error, on a no_price fill): no_live_source (Autoview has no live price for this market or venue; pass price, or set e= to a priced crypto venue), venue_read_failed (the venue's public ticker did not answer; retry, or pass price), price_ambiguous (price was sent with an alert that has more than one symbol; send one symbol per call). bad_price_param is the website's code for malformed price fields; it arrives as the refusal bad_price with price_error beside it.

Refusal codes (the whole call returns { error, code, fix }; do what fix says): command_required, command_and_order, bad_v3_line, bad_sandbox_id, order_missing_field, order_bad_field, bad_price, bad_price_source, bad_price_time, price_fields_without_price, sandbox_refused, sandbox_rate_limited, sandbox_bad_answer, sandbox_unreachable, sandbox_timeout, internal_error.

sandbox_id is minted when you omit it; pass it back to add more alerts to the same sandbox, and read them with sandbox_results. Any webhook sender can also POST alerts to webhook_url. Call pricing to see what going live costs.

Replaying past prices. To test a strategy on history, send one sandbox_run call per signal, oldest first. Set price to the price at that bar from your own data, price_source to where the data came from, and price_time to the bar's time. A past price_time is accepted; one more than a day in the future is refused (bad_price_time). Pass the sandbox_id from the first call on every later call, so all the fills land in one sandbox. Each fill uses your price as sent: fill.origin is caller, origin_note says the source and time are yours and not Autoview's quote, caller_price_time echoes the time you sent, and price_age_ms is how long before receipt that time was. A price more than 15 minutes old also gets price_warning, and the fill still counts. A limit your price has not reached comes back not_filled, and a later call does not fill it. Then call sandbox_results with the same sandbox_id: its book works out the position and realized P&L from the fills in the order they arrived, not by price_time. Every call counts toward the sandbox alert limits; on sandbox_rate_limited, do what fix says.

Fill model (every fill carries it as fill_model): each order fills at one snapshot price taken when the alert arrives, either the venue's public ticker (its best ask for a buy and best bid for a sell when the venue gives them, otherwise its last trade) or a price you supply (price, or fp= in the alert). A market order fills at that price. A marketable limit (a buy limit at or above it, a sell limit at or below it) fills at that price, never at the limit; any other limit stays open as not_filled and never fills later. The sandbox does not model order-book depth, slippage, latency or partial fills, and a caller price or last trade carries no spread, so live results will differ. fill.book_size is the size the venue's public ticker showed at that best ask or bid when the price was read, passed on as stored; it is not depth, it does not change the fill, and it is null when the price came with no size (a caller price, fp=, or a venue whose ticker gives none). For live-like execution, use the venue's own testnet or demo account through Autoview (pricing lists them with demo: true, at $0).

command.description: alert text, e.g. "e=kraken s=BTCUSD b=buy q=0.01" (classic key=value) or "buy(BTCUSD, 0.01)" (v3 line). Send this or order, not both

order.description: structured order (only these six fields; order.price is refused, use limit_price), rendered to the alert line "e=<exchange> s=<symbol> b=<side> q=<qty> t=<type>" (plus fp=<limit_price> for a limit); returned as compiled. Send this or command, not both

exchange.description: venue id, any spelling, e.g. "kraken", "oanda", "alpaca", "coinbase_advanced" (pricing with no exchanges lists every id)

symbol.description: one ticker with no spaces, as the venue writes it, e.g. "BTCUSD", "EURUSD", "AAPL"

qty.description: positive quantity in the venue's units, e.g. 0.01 (BTC), 1000 (EUR/USD units), 1 (shares)

limit_price.description: required when type is "limit": the limit price, e.g. 81000. Not the market price you read: that goes in the top-level price

exchange.description: venue id (any spelling) for a v3 line or alert text with no e=, e.g. "kraken"

sandbox_id.description: an existing sandbox id (32 lowercase hex, e.g. "6d43316194e3727e2411ef118974be1f") to reuse; omit to get a new one

price.description: optional current market price you read from your own user's data source for this symbol, e.g. 1.11419 or "1.11419" (positive number or decimal string). Used when Autoview has no price for the market; the fill is labelled caller-supplied. Not a limit price: for a limit use order.limit_price (or fp= in command). A price over 15 minutes old still fills, with fill.price_warning

price_source.description: optional, with price: where the price came from, up to 120 characters, e.g. "my OANDA practice account"

price_time.description: optional, with price: when it was read, ISO-8601 ("2026-10-28T17:00:00Z") or epoch milliseconds (1793206684433); not in the future

tools.name: sandbox_results
tools.description:
Read the simulated fills stored for a sandbox_id (from sandbox_run, or any Alert Sandbox webhook id), newest first. No token, no account, no key: simulation only, no real order was placed. Returns { sandbox: true, real_order_placed: false, notice, sandbox_id, alerts: [{ received_at, seq?, orders?: [same shape as sandbox_run orders, including fill.status (filled, not_filled, no_price or nothing_to_close), fill.origin, fill.price_label, fill.price_warning and fill.price_error], error? }], more, book, next_step } where alerts lists the newest 10 and more is true when older alerts exist beyond them. book = { positions: [{ exchange, symbol, net_qty, avg_entry, realized_pnl, last_fill_price, fills }], unvalued: [{ exchange, symbol, count }], unvalued_count, complete, method, note } is worked out on this call from up to 1000 stored alerts (an id with no account holds fewer, so it covers the whole store): average-cost, each market starting flat at its oldest fill read, no cash and no fees; net_qty is negative for a short and avg_entry is null when flat. Fills with no price or a percent qty are counted in unvalued and never valued; complete is false when older fills exist beyond the read. next_step = { market, practice_venue, practice_venue_name, same_venue, free, connect_url, text } names the free testnet or demo venue for the newest order's market and the page where your user connects it; practice_venue is null when Autoview has no match, and free is false when the only demo is not free to open. Pass text to your user as the next step. A refusal returns { error, code, fix }: bad_sandbox_id (malformed id), sandbox_refused (e.g. the id belongs to an account), sandbox_rate_limited, sandbox_bad_answer, sandbox_unreachable, sandbox_timeout, internal_error. Do what fix says.

Fill model (every fill carries it as fill_model): each order fills at one snapshot price taken when the alert arrives, either the venue's public ticker (its best ask for a buy and best bid for a sell when the venue gives them, otherwise its last trade) or a price you supply (price, or fp= in the alert). A market order fills at that price. A marketable limit (a buy limit at or above it, a sell limit at or below it) fills at that price, never at the limit; any other limit stays open as not_filled and never fills later. The sandbox does not model order-book depth, slippage, latency or partial fills, and a caller price or last trade carries no spread, so live results will differ. fill.book_size is the size the venue's public ticker showed at that best ask or bid when the price was read, passed on as stored; it is not depth, it does not change the fill, and it is null when the price came with no size (a caller price, fp=, or a venue whose ticker gives none). For live-like execution, use the venue's own testnet or demo account through Autoview (pricing lists them with demo: true, at $0).

sandbox_id.description: the sandbox id sandbox_run returned: 32 lowercase hex, e.g. "6d43316194e3727e2411ef118974be1f"

tools.name: paper_ledger
tools.description: Read a paper ledger back: its open positions, cash and the last fills, newest first. Nothing is sent to an exchange. Three forms. With paper_id (the id a no-token paper fill on entry returned) and no token: that one guest ledger, returned as { paper_ledger: true, exchange, cash, positions: [{ symbol, qty, avg_price, mark, mark_side, quote_at, unrealised_pnl }], fills: [{ symbol, side, qty, price, notional, bid, ask, quote_at, at }], more_fills, orders, note }. orders lists the ledger's newest paper limit orders, any state: [{ order_id, symbol, side, qty, limit_price, state (open, filled or cancelled), at, closed_at }]. Before it answers, the read asks the current quote for each symbol with an open order and fills each open order that quote crosses, at its limit price. Each position is marked at the current quote on its symbol: mark is the bid for a long and the ask for a short (mark_side says which), quote_at is when the quote was read, and unrealised_pnl is (mark - avg_price) x qty. Up to 10 symbols are quoted per ledger, each waiting up to 3 seconds; a position with no quote has mark, quote_at and unrealised_pnl null and a mark_reason (cap when the ledger holds more symbols than that, otherwise the quote's code, such as quote_timeout). With your user's Autoview account token and no paper_id: the account's own paper ledgers, one per exchange, as { paper_ledger: true, ledgers: [{ exchange, cash, positions, fills, more_fills }], note }; ledgers is empty when the account has none yet. With the token and a paper_id: that guest ledger moves onto the account (first claim wins; the reply carries claimed:true on the call that moved it) and is returned in the account form, ledgers holding just that one; this is the only form that writes, and once moved the paper_id no longer works without the token. qty is signed (negative is short); positions that are flat are left out; cash is null until a starting balance is set; amounts are in the symbol's quote currency. more_fills is true when older fills exist beyond limit. A refusal returns { error, code }: paper_id_unknown (no guest ledger has that paper_id), paper_id_other_exchange (exchange names another venue than the ledger's), paper_ledger_needs_id (neither paper_id nor a token), invalid_token, paper_exchange_out_of_scope (the token is not scoped for that exchange), paper_ledger_unavailable (try again shortly), paper_rate_limited (the paper_id form with no token is limited to 60 per hour from each connection, counted together with paper_reset; wait until retry_at), paper_id_claimed (with a token: another account already took that paper_id's ledger), paper_id_not_merged (with a token: the account already has its own paper ledger on that exchange, so it is kept, the guest ledger is not merged, and nothing changed).

token.description: your Autoview account token — an av_mcp_ personal access token, generate one at /account/tokens/ on the Autoview site. Omit this if your MCP client already sends it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header (Claude Code, Cursor, and most non-browser clients do this automatically once configured). With paper_id as well, it moves that guest ledger onto the account.

paper_id.description: the paper_id a no-token paper fill on entry returned, 32 hex characters; with no token reads that guest ledger, with a token moves it onto the account and reads it

exchange.description: optional: with a token, read only the ledger on this exchange (e.g. GEMINI); with paper_id, it must match the ledger's exchange

limit.description: how many of the newest fills to return, 1 to 100; defaults to 20

tools.name: paper_reset
tools.description: Start a paper ledger over with a starting balance: sets its cash to balance and clears its positions. Earlier fills stay in its history. Nothing is sent to an exchange. After a reset, each paper fill on that ledger moves cash: a buy takes its notional (quantity x price) from cash and a sell adds its notional; a buy that costs more than the cash fills nothing and entry returns paper_insufficient_cash. Without a reset cash stays null and every order fills. Two forms. With paper_id (the id a no-token paper fill on entry returned) and no token: that one guest ledger. With your user's Autoview account token and no paper_id: the account's paper ledger on exchange, which its first token fill on entry opened or a paper_id claim moved onto the account (paper_ledger_none if there is none). A paper_id claimed by an account no longer works here without the token: reset that ledger with the token form. It also cancels the ledger's open paper limit orders, so none of them fills later against the new cash. Returns { paper_reset: true, exchange, cash, positions: [], cancelled_orders (how many open orders it cancelled), note }. cash is in the quote currency of the symbols traded, unconverted. A refusal returns { error, code }: paper_reset_invalid (exchange missing, or balance not a positive number up to 1000000000000), paper_id_unknown (no guest ledger has that paper_id), paper_id_other_exchange (the ledger is on another exchange), paper_reset_needs_id (neither paper_id nor a token), invalid_token, paper_exchange_out_of_scope (the token is not scoped for that exchange), paper_ledger_none (the account has no paper ledger on that exchange), paper_ledger_unavailable (nothing changed; try again shortly), paper_rate_limited (the paper_id form with no token is limited to 60 per hour from each connection, counted together with paper_ledger; wait until retry_at).

token.description: your Autoview account token — an av_mcp_ personal access token, generate one at /account/tokens/ on the Autoview site. Omit this if your MCP client already sends it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header (Claude Code, Cursor, and most non-browser clients do this automatically once configured). Leave it out when you pass paper_id.

paper_id.description: the paper_id a no-token paper fill on entry returned, 32 hex characters; resets that guest ledger with no token. When paper_id is sent, the token is not used

exchange.description: the ledger's exchange, e.g. BINANCE; with paper_id it must match the ledger's exchange

balance.description: the starting cash, a positive number in the quote currency of the symbols you trade (e.g. 1000 for 1000 USDT on BTCUSDT)

tools.name: pricing
tools.description: What going live on Autoview costs, per venue. No token, no account: read-only, from Autoview's published price list. Each live exchange is its own subscription (most are $39.99 a month or $399.99 a year); practice/demo venues are free, and a few venues are free live. Returns { currency: "USD", venues: [{ exchange, name, live_monthly, live_yearly, demo, note, free_practice_venue?, live_venue? }], unknown?: [{ input, code: "unknown_exchange", fix }], how_to_go_live, source }. live_monthly and live_yearly are dollars (live_yearly is null when there is no yearly plan); demo is true for a practice venue (no real money, $0). Omit exchanges to list every venue. A refusal returns { error, code, fix }: bad_exchanges, too_many_exchanges, unknown_exchange. Do what fix says.

exchanges.description: optional venue ids, any spelling, up to 60, e.g. ["kraken", "oanda", "alpaca_paper"]; omit for every venue

tools.name: live_limits
tools.description: Read this token's live limits: the max order size and daily limit (USD notional: quantity x limit price, or quantity x trigger price when that is higher, or on a sell quantity x current bid when that is higher) your user set for this token, the account caps that cover every agent token on the account together (the hard outer limit once set; account.set is false when your user has not set them, and then the token's own caps alone apply), any tighter limits your user set for one exchange or one symbol on it (venue_caps, with today's use there), the most live orders this token may place in any rolling minute (max_orders_per_minute; null = no rate limit), how much of each is used today, and whether this token can place a live entry order right now. Read-only: an agent cannot set or raise these; only the user can, at /account/tokens/ (set_at). The day is the UTC calendar day (resets_at). Returns { live, max_order_usd, daily_limit_usd, used_today_usd, remaining_today_usd, account: { set, max_order_usd, daily_limit_usd, used_today_usd, remaining_today_usd }, effective_max_order_usd, effective_remaining_today_usd, venue_caps, max_orders_per_minute, agent_trading_paused, paused_at, token_paused, token_paused_at, day, resets_at, unit, set_at, can_place_live, code?, reason? }. agent_trading_paused true means your user has paused all agent trading on the account (code agent_trading_paused); only your user can turn it off. token_paused true means your user has paused this token (code agent_token_paused); only your user can turn it off. Tell your user these numbers before going live. Requires your Autoview account token.

token.description: your Autoview account token — an av_mcp_ personal access token, generate one at /account/tokens/ on the Autoview site. Omit this if your MCP client already sends it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header (Claude Code, Cursor, and most non-browser clients do this automatically once configured).

tools.name: alert
tools.description: Build everything TradingView's create_alert(webhook, message, expiration, resolution) needs, in one call: fuses `command` (the message) and `hooks` (the webhook URL for hook_id), and fills in the expiration (default 1 year out -- TradingView itself defaults to only 30 days, which silently stops the alert) and resolution (default "1") TradingView also needs. The order is validated against the exchange(s) hook_id is actually linked to and rejected if it could never fire there. Returns warnings you should read, including never putting the hook's key in the message field and a fan-out warning when the hook links more than one exchange. Pass the alert field instead of the structured fields to use raw webhook command text with any key a webhook accepts. Dry-run by default like `command`; set live:true to build a command that trades for real once the alert fires. For any other sender, `command` + `hooks` give the same message and webhook URL; expiration and resolution are TradingView settings only. Requires your Autoview account token.

token.description: your Autoview account token — an av_mcp_ personal access token, generate one at /account/tokens/ on the Autoview site. Omit this if your MCP client already sends it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header (Claude Code, Cursor, and most non-browser clients do this automatically once configured).

hook_id.description: the hook whose URL becomes the alert's webhook (see the `hooks` tool)

exchange.description: optional — any exchange id known to Autoview (see `catalog`); a bracket is refused if that exchange lists its params as unsupported. Must be one of the exchanges hook_id is linked to (otherwise the alert is rejected); omit to validate against every exchange the hook is linked to

alert.description: the raw command text a webhook body carries, e.g. s=BTCUSD b=buy q=0.01 fp=60000 ef=any tif=gtc; any key a webhook accepts works here, it is checked by the engine's parser and becomes the message as-is (with d=1 leading each line unless live is true). Do not combine with the structured order fields.

symbol.description: the instrument symbol, e.g. EUR_USD, XBTUSD, BTC_USD. Required unless alert is set

action.description: manage EXISTING orders/positions on symbol instead of placing a new one: cancel = cancel open orders, close = close open positions, flat = cancel every order AND close every position (Tradovate only). When set, side (if given) is an optional buy/sell filter (not applicable to flat), and quantity/type/price/trigger/brackets/unit are ignored.

side.description: order direction; required unless action is set, where it is an optional buy/sell filter for cancel/close (omit for flat)

quantity.description: order size: a positive number (contracts/units), or a percent-of-balance string like "50%" (1-100%). Required unless action is set.

type.description: order type; defaults to limit at the ticker (t=limit with no price, same as a plain alert). An attached bracket needs type market explicitly.

price.description: absolute limit price; required for an explicit limit, post_only, ioc, fok, and stop_limit (omit type and price for a limit at the ticker)

trigger.description: absolute trigger (stop) price; required for stop and stop_limit

priceRef.description: reference price for percent sizing and brackets

sizeAgainstEquity.description: for a percent quantity, size against equity instead of available balance (y=equity)

unit.description: "currency" treats quantity as a CURRENCY amount to convert to units at the resolved price (u=currency) — e.g. quantity:10 with unit:"currency" on BTC/USD buys $10 of BTC instead of 10 BTC. Only meaningful with a fixed (non-percent) quantity.

stopLoss.description: attached bracket stop-loss distance from the fill: points (10) or a percent string such as 3%; a sign, if given, must point the right way); pairs with takeProfit or a trail leg

takeProfit.description: attached bracket take-profit distance from the fill: points (20) or a percent string such as 5%; pairs with stopLoss or a trail leg

trailStop.description: auto-trail stop distance in points; requires trailActivate

trailActivate.description: points of profit before the trail starts; required whenever trailStop is set

trailFrequency.description: how often the trailing stop re-checks price; defaults to 1 if omitted

live.description: false (default) = build a dry-run preview command (appends d=1); true = build a command that places a real order when the alert fires

expiration.description: ISO 8601 timestamp for TradingView's alert expiration; defaults to 1 year from now

resolution.description: chart timeframe TradingView's create_alert needs; defaults to "1" (1 minute)

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Send your user's feedback to the Autoview team: a feature request, a bug report, a question, or anything else. Works with no account and no token (as a guest), or with your user's token. Each message is saved for a person to review before it goes to the team; there is no set response time. With a token, the account is attached on our side from the token, so do not add it. Never put passwords, API keys or other secrets in message. If your user wants an answer, put a way to reach them in contact (for example an email address), or with a token set contact to true to use the address on the account. Show your user the message and get their go-ahead before sending. message is up to 4000 characters. Limit: 2 per hour for each account, or for each guest. Returns { received, id, status, guest, remaining_this_hour, note }; pass note to your user. A refusal returns { error, code, fix }: bad_kind, message_empty, message_too_long, contact_too_long, invalid_token, feedback_rate_limited (with retry_at), feedback_unavailable, feedback_store_failed. Do what fix says.

token.description: your Autoview account token — an av_mcp_ personal access token, generate one at /account/tokens/ on the Autoview site. Omit this if your MCP client already sends it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header (Claude Code, Cursor, and most non-browser clients do this automatically once configured). Optional here: leave it out to send as a guest.

message.description: your user's feedback in their own words, up to 4000 characters. For a bug, say what was sent, what happened and what was expected; a trace or canonical_id from events helps.

contact.description: optional: how to reach your user if they want a reply (for example an email address, up to 254 characters), or true to use the address on the account (token only). Omit for no reply.

tools.name: feedback_status
tools.description: Read where one send_feedback message stands: pending (waiting for a person to review it), approved (passed on to the Autoview team) or declined (reviewed and not passed on), with received_at. Pass the id send_feedback returned and the same account token it was sent with. Only the status comes back, never the message or contact. Feedback sent without a token has no status to read. Returns { id, status, received_at, note }. A refusal returns { error, code, fix }: bad_id, not_found (no such id for this account; the same answer for an id that belongs to someone else), invalid_token, feedback_unavailable. Do what fix says.

token.description: your Autoview account token — an av_mcp_ personal access token, generate one at /account/tokens/ on the Autoview site. Omit this if your MCP client already sends it as an `Authorization: Bearer` header (Claude Code, Cursor, and most non-browser clients do this automatically once configured). Use the token the feedback was sent with.

id.description: the id send_feedback returned (a UUID such as 01a1c64b-0000-7000-8000-000000000000)
